public_rationale: The January 23, 2023 announcement described Azure as the exclusive cloud provider for all OpenAI workloads [e1]. The October 28, 2025 agreement reduced exclusivity: it allowed non-API products developed with third parties on other clouds and removed Microsoft's compute right of first refusal [e2]. But that agreement also extended Microsoft's model and product IP rights through 2032, including post-AGI models, and added a $250 billion Azure purchase commitment [e3]. For the October–December 2025 assessment period, reduced exclusivity supports weakening in that respect; the stronger contractual commitments count against an unqualified claim that the relationship weakened [e2][e3].
limitations: Public contractual terms do not establish private trust or personal relations.
The evidence provides no common measure for weighing reduced exclusivity against stronger continuing commitments.
